skill.name: neuropixels-analysis
skill.description: Guides Neuropixels extracellular electrophysiology workflows with SpikeInterface, including loading, preprocessing, motion correction, spike sorting, metrics, curation, visualization, and export.
skill.summary: Analyze Neuropixels recordings from raw data through curated spike-sorting results.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 101 static findings were adjudicated. The static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder API keys, documentation URLs, scientific domain terms, and expected output writes. One semantic privacy risk remains because AI-assisted curation may send derived neural data to external model providers.

remediation.issue: External AI-assisted curation may disclose derived research data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sending plots or metadata to model APIs, and document what data leaves the local environment.

remediation.issue: API client examples show hardcoded placeholder keys.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or secret managers in examples so users do not copy hardcoded key patterns into notebooks.

remediation.issue: Installation examples reference moving third-party packages and GitHub repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend pinned package versions or verified releases for reproducible and safer scientific environments.

remediation.issue: Bundled scripts write analysis artifacts to user-selected output directories.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to choose dedicated output directories and avoid paths containing important existing files.

content.value_statement: Neuropixels analysis requires many linked preprocessing, sorting, and curation steps. This skill provides practical SpikeInterface workflows, scripts, and references for reproducible neural recording analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading SpikeGLX, Open Ephys, and NWB recordings with SpikeInterface.
Documents preprocessing steps for filtering, phase shift correction, bad channels, and common median reference.
Explains drift estimation and non-rigid motion correction workflows.
Provides Kilosort4, SpykingCircus2, and Mountainsort5 spike sorting examples.
Includes scripts for preprocessing, sorting, quality metrics, and Phy export.
Documents Allen, IBL, and strict quality metric curation thresholds.
limitations: Requires external neuroscience Python packages, and some sorters require a GPU.
Example scripts assume local recording paths and may need lab-specific adaptation.
Does not replace expert review of uncertain units or scientific conclusions.
AI-assisted curation can share plots with selected model providers if users enable it.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Recording
use_cases.description: Load a SpikeGLX or Open Ephys session, inspect channels, apply preprocessing, and save reusable intermediate data.

use_cases.title: Run a Sorting Pipeline
use_cases.description: Choose a sorter, run postprocessing, compute quality metrics, and export results for manual review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Unit Curation
use_cases.description: Apply Allen, IBL, or strict criteria across sessions and document thresholds for reproducible analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Preprocessing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local recording folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a Neuropixels SpikeGLX recording at [path]. Help me plan safe preprocessing, expected outputs, and checks before spike sorting.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Motion Correction
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a drift workflow after initial inspection.
prompt_templates.prompt: My drift plot shows [describe pattern]. Recommend a motion correction strategy and explain which parameters I should inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sorter Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Pick a sorter for available compute and study goals.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to sort a Neuropixels recording with [hardware limits]. Compare Kilosort4, SpykingCircus2, and Mountainsort5 for this case.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Curation Criteria
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of quality thresholds and reproducibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these quality metric thresholds and curation labels for a Neuropixels study. Identify weak assumptions and suggest a reproducible reporting plan.

output_examples.input: Plan preprocessing for a Neuropixels 1.0 SpikeGLX recording.
output: Load the AP stream and confirm channel count, duration, and sampling rate.
Apply high-pass filtering, phase shift correction, bad channel removal, and common median reference.
Save the preprocessed recording in a new output directory and keep the raw data unchanged.
Generate drift and probe layout plots before selecting a sorter.

output_examples.input: Help interpret quality metrics after Kilosort4.
output: Separate obvious noise units using low SNR and poor presence ratio.
Flag units with refractory period violations for manual review.
Compare Allen, IBL, and strict thresholds before declaring final good units.
Export uncertain units to Phy when the experiment depends on precise curation.

output_examples.input: Create a reporting checklist for a completed analysis.
output: Record probe type, preprocessing parameters, sorter version, and motion correction settings.
Summarize total units, accepted units, rejected units, and key quality metric distributions.
Include drift plots, waveform summaries, correlograms, and curation criteria in the methods record.

best_practices: Inspect drift and bad channels before spike sorting, especially for long recordings.
Save preprocessed data and parameter records so analyses can be reproduced.
Use automated curation as a first pass and manually review borderline units.
anti_patterns: Running spike sorting on raw data without checking drift, probe metadata, or bad channels.
Treating quality metric thresholds as universal across probes, brain regions, and experiments.
Sending plots or metadata to external AI services without confirming data governance rules.

faq.question: Does this skill run spike sorting by itself?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and scripts. Users still run the commands in their own Python environment.

faq.question: Which data formats are covered?
faq.answer: The documentation covers SpikeGLX, Open Ephys, and NWB workflows through SpikeInterface.

faq.question: Do I need a GPU?
faq.answer: Kilosort4 benefits from a GPU. CPU-based alternatives such as SpykingCircus2 and Mountainsort5 are also discussed.

faq.question: Can this replace manual curation?
faq.answer: No. It supports automated and AI-assisted review, but important or uncertain units still need expert inspection.

faq.question: Does it handle motion correction?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains drift checks, SpikeInterface presets, and non-rigid correction options for Neuropixels recordings.

faq.question: What should I check before using AI-assisted curation?
faq.answer: Confirm whether plots or derived recording data can be shared with the selected model provider.
